active_themes.label: Powell Timeline Pressure
active_themes.summary: Warsh confirmation still on procedural track; no direct news today. Geopolitical relief (Iran ceasefire signals, oil retreat from $100+) has reduced acute May deadline pressure on Powell. The underlying structural issue persists: markets will test whether Fed policy decisions—particularly on rate cuts and timing—are made under political duress rather than data independence. Today's jobs beat (115K, double expectations) removes one near-term pressure valve, but lender de-risking suggests institutions are already assuming institutional erosion.

active_themes.label: Iran Ceasefire Holding
active_themes.summary: Oil retreated from $100+ on renewed ceasefire signals, validating the 3-week assumption that escalation risk is real but negotiable. The structural test remains: whether the next escalatory event (vessel seizure, drone strike, strait blockade) breaks the framework or holds within bounds. Markets are pricing ceasefire-with-elevated-oil ($85–95 range) as base case. The cost to households and corporate margins is already embedded in credit markets through lender behavior, not yet in employment data.

active_themes.label: Decisions Made Under Threat
active_themes.summary: Apple's 15bp savings rate cut (today) is the second major institutional move in 14 days confirming lenders are retreating before a consumer shock hits. These moves are rational de-risking: institutions are pricing energy-shock inflation expectations and reducing consumer credit exposure in advance of potential employment weakness. When credit tightens before employment falls, spending multipliers amplify the downturn. The mechanism is observable and repeating.

active_themes.label: Lender De-risking Accelerates
active_themes.summary: Apple rate cut today, federal student loan collapse last week—two separate institutions, same signal. Lenders are de-risking in advance of a consumer shock they expect but do not yet see in employment data. If inflation holds and employment stays strong, credit tightening is a non-event. If either weakens, reduced credit availability becomes a spending multiplier that turns a moderate downturn into a sharper one.

open_watchlist.meaning: This signals real inflation expectations are rising and equities are repricing higher discount rates; the AI/tech narrative cannot overcome inflation-shock fundamentals.

open_watchlist.meaning: Negotiation signal fails; oil reprices to $100+; Treasury yields spike; equity rally reverses within 48 hours and credit tightening becomes systemic multiplier.

open_watchlist.meaning: Inflation expectations are re-anchoring higher despite geopolitical relief; real yields are rising; Fed pressure intensifies and Warsh confirmation becomes flash point for Fed independence narrative.
